"We have a damage report naming your ship."

"Hegemony Navy. Heave to."

"$entity.catchrelease_harpoonFineDGS credits."

"Pay it and this remains an accident report."

"Corporate security."

"Pay it."

"Hold up."

$PersonName grins.

The grin broadens.

"Very funny story. Expensive story."

"$entity.catchrelease_harpoonFineDGS and we're even."

$PersonRank $personName has assembled several statutes into a workable stack.

$personName looks at a damage report.

"Restaurants, private kitchens, two mess halls and somebody on the orbital who will pay extra if I stop asking what they do with it."

"Yes."

A young factor in an expensive jacket is giving a presentation to a slate propped against an empty chair.

"You fish. Good."

He moves a sales projection aside.

"I have buyers for fresh catch. What I don't have is a supplier willing to put their name on a repeat delivery schedule."

He shows you the first order.

"$catchreleaseAskCap. One demonstration shipment."

"$catchreleaseRewardCap. If it arrives when you say it will, I can sell the second run before the first is unpacked."

text:
"Excellent."

He sends an invoice template.

"Fill in whatever parts fishermen fill in."

"Fine. Entirely fine."

He turns back to the empty chair.

"Where were we?"
"Still need the demonstration shipment. $catchreleaseAskCap."

He photographs the containers, the handling seals, and you standing beside both.

$catchreleaseReward is transferred immediately.

The first shipment has apparently become a presentation.

"I need the next run."

He sends the new quantity.

"$catchreleaseAskCap. Same buyer, more tables."

He stares at the signed delivery receipt.

"Repeat customer."

Then, more quietly:

"Good."
A man in a well-cut coat sits with an untouched drink and the patient posture of someone paid to wait.

"I purchase for a private household."

He does not volunteer the name.

"The request is $catchreleaseAsk."

He checks the wording once.

"It is for display, not the kitchen. Condition matters less than meeting the specification."

"$catchreleaseRewardCap on presentation."

"Very good."

No contact details are exchanged. Your mission log nevertheless updates.
"Understood."
"The requirement remains $catchreleaseAskCap."

He checks the container seal, then the scale.

"That will do."

$catchreleaseRewardCap changes hands.
A woman with an academic lanyard and salt-damaged hands is annotating photographs of public aquaria.

"I run a collection."

She turns the slate around.

"Public-facing, grant-funded, technically conservation."

She points to the requested entry.

"$catchreleaseAsk."

"A clean specimen is useful for the display. A badly deformed one is useful for the records. I'm not going to reject either because it failed to look picturesque."

"$catchreleaseRewardCap."

text: "Keep the transport tank stable. The exhibit system can handle the rest."

"Good. Thank you."

Two children occupy a corner table they are almost certainly not paying for. One has a bucket. The other has a handwritten tournament bracket.

"We need two."

The child with the bracket speaks for both.

"For the championship."

The bucket is turned toward you. It is empty.

"$catchreleaseAskCap. One each."

You point out that fish are not generally known for organized combat.

"That's why we need good ones."

The offered payment is $catchreleaseReward. Between them, it appears to be all the money they have.

text:
Your sensors officer picks a cold hull out of the debris field: an old auxiliary stripped farther than a salvage crew would ordinarily bother.

One object remains attached to the dorsal handling deck.

At first it reads as part of the ship. Closer inspection resolves a reinforced servicing frame with maneuvering thrusters, a dead transponder, and mounting points sized for something not much smaller than a fighter.

The frame is held to the wreck by three emergency clamps. None belong to the wreck.

text:
The boarding party finds an ordinary dead ship.

The reactor is cold. The lockers have been emptied. Someone took the expensive avionics and left the galley fittings. There are no bodies.

Your ops chief sends back imagery of the external frame.

"Different story out here. LYNE markings. Fisheries service codes, maybe. Half of them don't resolve against anything in the registry."

A closer image follows.

Someone has scratched maintenance intervals into the casing by hand.

Your crew can recover the assembly intact. It will take a cargo crane and several hours of unproductive swearing.

The transponder package still contains the last service handshake it accepted.

The source is listed simply as FISHERMAN.

"Not like that. We were doing a transfer. Skipper thought I was aboard the tender. Tender thought I was aboard the ship. Everybody signed the same manifest and left."

He points to the beacon.

"By the time anyone worked it out, I wasn't on their route anymore."

He drinks from the water pouch your people gave him.

"Worked around the Fisherman's boats. If you're looking for them, go past the settled traffic and hail the trawlers."

text:
The trawler answers without ceremony.

The Fisherman is at a worktable with a mug in one hand and a dismantled control unit under the other.

"Evening, captain. Buying, selling, or looking for work?"

"Back again."

The Fisherman pushes something out of frame.

"Got range data if you need it. Got work if you don't."

A crewman crosses behind him carrying a sealed crate. Halfway across the compartment there is no longer a crate in his hands.

The Fisherman's voice reaches the bridge a moment before the comm indicator turns green.

"Evening."

When the picture follows, he is pouring something into the same battered mug.

"What's the trouble?"

The link opens on the Fisherman watching somebody work off-screen.

"Easy with that."

A metallic impact follows from your left audio channel, though the trawler lies to starboard.

He looks back to you.

"Captain. What can I do for you?"

The Fisherman glances at the salvage manifest attached to your catch log.

"Bycatch."

He taps the entry once.

"Wreckage. Lost cargo. Whatever the retrieval rig brings up with the pattern."

The hail is accepted promptly.

An older man in patched working clothes studies your transponder return. Grey stubble, old scar tissue, the posture of someone who spent enough years on command decks to stop sitting properly in chairs.

"Haven't got you in the ledger."

He takes a drink.

"That's usually how new work starts."

The trawler cuts across your approach before you get much closer to the unstable fabric.

The Fisherman comes on the channel.

"Easy."

He looks at your ship, then toward the rupture.

"You've no ROD aboard. Another hundred klicks and I'll have to come fetch you instead of your catch."

He gestures away from it.

"Come alongside."

"That's the one."

text:
"Cut the lights."

$PersonRank $personName has your sensor signature on another display.

"Whatever rig you're running is throwing interference across $entity.catchrelease_lampWhere and the inhabited approaches around it."

"This is the warning. Power it down."

"Hegemony Navy. Shut the device down."

$PersonRank $personName reads the order.

"Unlicensed high-energy operation within a protected navigation volume."

The card is lowered.

"Kill the lights."

"Corporate security."

A clean sensor plot appears beside $personName.

"Your equipment is producing effects outside your licensed operating envelope."

A polite smile.

"There is no licensed operating envelope."

"Power down."

"Extinguish it."

$PersonRank $personName looks past your bridge image toward the lamps.

"You were not given creation to cut at until something answers."

A small shake of the head.

"Put it away from the inhabited."

"Turn it off."

No formal introduction follows.

"Then jettison it."

A pause.

"If you need us to choose the order, we will."

"Kill the lights."

$personName points at a traffic plot.

"You are lighting up half our scopes and upsetting people who pay us specifically not to be upset."

"Do it somewhere emptier."

"Cease operation."

$PersonRank $personName reads the legal header.

"Unauthorized high-energy apparatus within Diktat-controlled space."

"The first order is to shut it down."

"League patrol. Please power down the device."

$PersonRank $personName checks the notice.

"Unlicensed operation inside inhabited approaches. First instance: warning."

The notice disappears.

"That's the warning."

"Hey. Lights off."

$personName looks at the sensor plot.

"I don't know what you've built. I know every instrument near $entity.catchrelease_lampWhere noticed it."

"Take it somewhere nobody lives."

"You've had the warning."

The previous incident sits open beside the new one.

"$entity.catchrelease_lampFineDGS credits. Pay it and shut the rig down."

"Second recorded operation."

"$entity.catchrelease_lampFineDGS credits."

"Pay. Power down. Leave."

"Repeat incident."

The settlement value appears.

"$entity.catchrelease_lampFineDGS."

"Further recurrence moves this out of billing."

"You were asked once."

"The fine is $entity.catchrelease_lampFineDGS credits."

"Pay it. Put the lights out."

"You kept it."

The speaker looks at the equipment feed.

"$entity.catchrelease_lampFineDGS if you want the administrative version."

"Otherwise we come over."

"Twice costs money."

"$entity.catchrelease_lampFineDGS."

"Next time costs ships."

"Second offense."

"The statutory penalty is $entity.catchrelease_lampFineDGS credits."

"There is no statutory third warning."

"Second recorded instance."

"$entity.catchrelease_lampFineDGS credits."

$PersonRank $personName closes the notice.

"Please do not make me find out what the third section means."

"You again."

$personName puts the figure on-screen.

"$entity.catchrelease_lampFineDGS. Lights off."

"I'd like this to be the last time I learn something new about fishing."

"Cut the lamps and prepare for inspection."

$PersonRank $personName has stopped discussing the device.

"We are boarding for the equipment and anything recovered during the violation."

"Hegemony Navy. Heave to and prepare to be boarded."

"Repeated operation of prohibited equipment. Recovery cargo will be inspected and seized where applicable."

"Your operating privilege, insofar as one ever existed, has been withdrawn."

"Stand by for inspection."

"Power it down."

The boarding order follows.

"What you brought back while using it will not remain aboard your ship."
"Drives cold. Lamps cold. Hands where the boarding party can see them."

"All right. We're done asking."

A boarding shuttle separates from the formation.

"Third offense. Heave to."

The order contains no settlement amount.

"The convention has run out of warnings and fines."

$PersonRank $personName looks at the boarding authorization.

"Prepare to be boarded."

"I told you I didn't want to learn more about this."

A boarding authorization appears.

"Apparently I do."

text:
"You are entering a contracted exclusion zone. The rupture is off limits to fishing operations."

$PersonRank $personName sends over a file number.

"Client identity is protected. The relocation figure is $entity.catchrelease_campBribeDGS credits. Otherwise, alter course."

The woman on the screen stands in front of somebody armed.

"Do not lower your machine into that rupture. This place is closed to fishing."

Her voice remains level.

"You can offer $entity.catchrelease_campBribeDGS credits. We may take it. That changes where we stand, not what the machine is."

"You've come about the fishing spot."

Whoever answers checks your fleet before continuing.

"We're using it. You want us somewhere else, $entity.catchrelease_campBribeDGS credits makes somewhere else worth the trouble."

"Well. Somebody actually came out."

The pirate looks toward the rupture.

"Nice bit of empty space. No patrols, no customs, no traffic unless somebody wants the fishing."

$HeOrShe looks back to you.

"$entity.catchrelease_campBribeDGS buys us another quiet place. Otherwise this one's occupied."

"Contracted denial of the site."

$PersonRank $personName sends over a file number.

"Client identity is protected. Our instruction is simply that fishing operations do not resume while the contract remains active."

The buyout figure appears.

"$entity.catchrelease_campBribeDGS. Above that, relocation is cheaper than remaining on station."

The woman on the screen stands in front of somebody armed.

"You came for the fishing."

Her eyes move briefly toward the rupture.

"We have watched crews bring their machines here and lower them into places no human hand should reach. We are stopping the work."

The payment figure is already known.

"You can offer $entity.catchrelease_campBribeDGS. We may even take it. That changes where we stand, not what the machine is."

notes: Greyed out with a reason rather than hidden, the way vanilla handles a bribe the player cannot cover.

text:
You do not argue ownership.

Instead you run through the ordinary hazards of holding station over an unstable rupture: drone losses, sensor failures, poor recovery rates, and the expense of getting a damaged fleet back to a real yard.

The person on the screen listens to the numbers.

Eventually:

"We were moving on anyway."

The formation comes about.
